summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her scheduled cycle of high-dose methotrexate but reported mild gastrointestinal discomfort following a recent barbecue. Due to her history of colonic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, a CT abdomen was performed, revealing jejunal wall thickening concerning for either infection or lymphomatous involvement. Methotrexate was held, and she was started on empiric antibiotics. An upper enteroscopy showed only mild gastritis with normal small bowel mucosa, though the area of concern was not reached. Her symptoms resolved, stool studies were negative for pathogens including C. difficile, and she improved clinically. She was discharged on a short course of antibiotics with plans to follow up with GI and undergo a PET scan to further evaluate for disease recurrence. Her chemotherapy was deferred pending further results.
